newsitem.title: USA: Dade County Mayor backs new airport.
newsitem.headline: Dade County Mayor backs new airport.

text.p: The mayor of Dade County Tuesday night spoke strongly in favor of building a new airport in southern Florida, despite enviornmentalists' concerns about the location of the airport and the impact it might have on the Everglades and Biscayne Bay.

"I understand the concerns that have been raised by environmentalists," Mayor Alex Penelas said. He told a meeting of the National Association of Women Business owners that the proposed site, the Homestaed Air Reserve Base, is the most appropriate place to build another airport.
Formerly Homestead Air Force Base, the facility south of Miami was severely damaged by Hurricane Andrew in 1992 and subsequently was downgraded to an air reserve base.

Metro-Dade County Commissioners in January voted to award a lease to develop the Homestead base into another airport to serve Miami. Environmentalists have asked for another environmental impact study, threatening to sue if development begins without one.
"Apart from the Air Base, the Everglades is the only other place in the county we could build another airport. So we must mover forward with a new airport at Homestead Air Force base," Penelas said.
"We are facing a critical need for a second regional airport in Dade County," he said.
